group: Payment apps that lend to shops
how_they_reach_the_owner: A free QR code and speaker at the counter
how_they_earn: Shop loans repaid from daily sales. PhonePe arranges them with 56 lenders; BharatPe also lends from its own NBFC
key_fact: PhonePe arranged Rs 4,507 cr of shop loans in FY25 and earned Rs 328 cr on them. Paytm has 1.57 cr shops paying for a device (Jun 2026)
key_fact_source: Business Today (Mar 2026); Paytm Q1 FY27 release
where_they_beat_us: They see every sale on their QR and take the instalment out of it. Huge reach and field staff.
where_we_beat_them: Each sees one QR of about 9. Only about 1 in 4 registered PhonePe shops use it in a month. Savings is a side line: Paytm calls its fund and gold revenue 'negligible'.

how_they_reach_the_owner: Daily auto-debit into debt funds from Rs 100; paid agents (Bachatt Partner) sign up savers
how_they_earn: Fund commission, plus referral fees on loans up to Rs 5 lakh from 7 lenders and on credit cards
key_fact: $16M raised (Accel, Lightspeed, Info Edge). Claims 3M users. Has published no retention, loan or default figure
where_they_beat_us: About 17 months and $15M ahead, with an agent network, on the same customer.
where_we_beat_them: Refers loans only, and has published none of the three numbers.

players: PhonePe Daily SIP, Jar, Gullak, Paytm Money
how_they_reach_the_owner: Daily saving from Rs 10 (funds or digital gold) inside a consumer app
how_they_earn: Gold margin (Jar), fund commission, then insurance and loans
key_fact: PhonePe Daily SIP: 5 lakh+ investors in 8 months, 77% from tier-2 and tier-3 towns. Jar: 35M registered users, Rs 208 cr operating revenue in FY25 (its own definition)
where_they_beat_us: Cheaper to start (Rs 10), bigger brands, already on the owner's phone.
where_we_beat_them: Built for young consumers, not for a shop's money needs: no business loans or shop cover around the saving.

group: The cash agent and the credit co-op
players: Daily-deposit (pigmy) agents, credit co-op societies, chit funds, bank daily-deposit schemes
how_they_reach_the_owner: An agent comes to the counter every day and takes cash
how_they_earn: Lending margin on loans to members; the agent earns a commission
key_fact: Maharashtra alone: 2 lakh+ daily agents serving about 1 crore families; about 2 lakh credit co-ops nationally
where_they_beat_us: Cash, face to face, and a loan from the same society. This is the habit we must replace.
where_we_beat_them: Low interest, a penalty for taking money out early, and no deposit insurance. Sahara repaid 27 lakh of 1.35 crore depositors by Jul 2025.

how_they_earn: Interest on their own loan book
key_fact: Lendingkart's loan book fell 74% and revenue 62% to Rs 327 cr in FY26; NeoGrowth's book fell about 21%
where_they_beat_us: They lend from their own money and set their own terms.
where_we_beat_them: They are retreating after bad loans rose, and have no daily contact with the owner. They could become our lenders.

how_they_reach_the_owner: Branches in every market; no income proof needed
how_they_earn: Interest on loans secured by gold
key_fact: Rs 19.4 lakh crore gold-loan book (Mar 2026), up from Rs 6.3 lakh crore in 2023; average loan Rs 1.96 lakh
where_we_beat_them: They need gold and a branch visit, and do nothing for saving. Better as a partner product than a rival.

how_they_reach_the_owner: A business bank account, invoicing or a credit ledger the owner opens every day
how_they_earn: Fees, subscriptions and loan referrals (Tide works with about 25 lenders)
key_fact: Tide: 800,000+ Indian businesses by Sep 2025, over half of its 1.6M members worldwide
where_they_beat_us: They see the business's books and money too. Tide also offers fixed deposits.
where_we_beat_them: None runs daily saving; they serve the business, we serve the owner's own money. We found no reliable recent figures for Khatabook.

group: Supplier credit and gig platforms (side slices)
players: udaanCapital and FMCG ordering apps; Swiggy, Urban Company
how_they_reach_the_owner: Credit at the moment the shop buys stock; loans and saving inside a gig app
key_fact: udaanCapital: Rs 8,000 cr a year to 1.5 lakh kiranas (2022). Swiggy rider loans Rs 102 cr (2023); Swiggy x Zerodha saving from Rs 100 (Jun 2026)
key_fact_source: Northern Arc release (2022); Business Standard (Dec 2023); Outlook Business
where_they_beat_us: Credit exactly when it is needed, with repayment built into the next order or payout.
where_we_beat_them: Narrow: one supplier's stock or one platform's payout.
